payload.lessonGoal: Explain why KV cache dominates long-context serving costs and how CED plus CSA2 reduce global and persistent footprints to one-quarter and one-eighth respectively.
payload.learnerAssumption: Student understands basic Transformer attention but not specific cache compression techniques or DeepSeek architecture details.
payload.centralQuestion: How do architectural changes shrink the massive memory footprint required for million-token context serving?

requiredClaims.statement: Large KV caches strain HBM and SSD capacity, creating primary bottlenecks for deployment costs.
Causal Encoder-Decoder activates only 8B parameters during prefill versus 16B during decode.
CSA2 and FP4 caching reduce global KV cache footprint to roughly one-quarter of previous models.
SWA Bounded Replay reduces persistent KV cache footprint to roughly one-eighth of previous models.

requiredMechanisms.statement: Decoder global KV is projected from final encoder hidden states, bypassing full decoder computation during prefill.
Compressed Sparse Attention 2 shares main KV and indexer K across layers to reduce duplicated storage.
SWA Bounded Replay reconstructs missing sliding window states by replaying only recent tokens instead of persisting them.

scenes.teachingGoal: Demonstrate how CED projection and CSA2 reuse shrink runtime cache, while SWA replay shrinks persistent storage.
scenes.learnerShouldUnderstand: The system compresses memory usage through architectural sharing and approximate reconstruction rather than just quantization.
scenes.mentalModel: A multi-layered storage system where data flows from encoder to decoder, gets shared across layers, and is selectively reconstructed on demand.

beats.purpose: Establish the problem: large KV caches dominate memory costs in long-context serving.
beats.narrationDraft: Long-context agents generate massive key-value caches that strain high-bandwidth memory and solid-state drive capacity simultaneously.

beats.purpose: Introduce Causal Encoder-Decoder as the first mechanism reducing prefill compute and cache generation.
beats.narrationDraft: The causal encoder-decoder projects decoder keys directly from encoder outputs, halving active parameters during input processing.

beats.purpose: Explain how CSA2 shares KV entries across layers to reduce duplicated storage significantly.
beats.narrationDraft: Compressed sparse attention shares main key-value vectors across multiple layers, eliminating redundant storage within the network.

beats.purpose: Quantify the global cache reduction achieved by combining CED, CSA2, and FP4 precision.
beats.narrationDraft: These architectural choices shrink the global cache footprint to eight hundred ninety bytes per token, roughly one quarter of before.

beats.purpose: Introduce SWA Bounded Replay as the solution for persistent cache storage on slower media.
beats.narrationDraft: Sliding window attention bounded replay avoids storing local states permanently by reconstructing them from recent tokens only.

beats.purpose: Quantify the persistent cache reduction achieved by removing SWA storage requirements.
beats.narrationDraft: Removing sliding window storage from persistent memory reduces the total disk footprint to roughly one eighth of the baseline model.

beats.purpose: Synthesize the combined impact of all mechanisms on deployment cost and performance.
beats.narrationDraft: Together these optimizations ease pressure on hardware capacity while delivering better overall performance than the larger predecessor model.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache compression relies solely on lower precision formats like FP4.
misconceptions.correction: Compression primarily comes from architectural sharing via CSA2 and CED projection, with FP4 providing secondary gains.

misconceptions.claim: Persistent cache stores all attention states indefinitely.
misconceptions.correction: Persistent cache excludes sliding window states, which are reconstructed on demand using bounded replay.
